    • Configure the support link with QABOARD_SUPPORT_URL.
    • Tell users which credentials to use when they can't log in, with QABOARD_LOGIN_HINT, and where to install WebCDE, which opens runs with a cde.sh, with QABOARD_WEBCDE_INSTALLER (environment variables). The tuning form's feedback link goes to QABOARD_SUPPORT_URL.
    • Email users when the batches they start end: set QABOARD_SMTP_HOST, and optionally the sender, reply-to address and email domain (QABOARD_EMAIL_FROM, QABOARD_EMAIL_REPLY_TO, QABOARD_EMAIL_DOMAIN). A migration adds a batch_notifications table and an index of the pending runs, built without blocking writes (emails).
    • Scripts can send results that describe their commit with only commit_sha and commit_authored_datetime: the other commit_* fields (branch, message, committer, parents) are optional, and the server doesn't need access to the git repository.
  • Database: faster commit lists, safer migrations, tunable PostgreSQL.
    • Lists of commits answer many times faster on big projects, and use much less memory: they no longer load every output of every commit.
    • Adds two indexes on ci_commits, to list commits faster. They are built without blocking writes, which can take a few minutes on big databases. If building one fails, the next deploy builds it again.
    • Starts even when the database has migrations it doesn't know, made by a newer version, e.g. after a rollback: it keeps them.
    • Tune PostgreSQL with a settings file: use services/db/init.sh as the database's entrypoint and it includes services/db/qaboard.conf (or your own, QABOARD_DB_CONFIG) in PostgreSQL's configuration at every start, and in new databases right away, with the pg_stat_statements extension (database settings).
    • Size the backend's database connection pools with QABOARD_DB_POOL_SIZE and QABOARD_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW (default 4 and 2 per uwsgi process, instead of 10 and 5): PostgreSQL's max_connections can stay small. The backend checks connections before using them, so it keeps working after a restart of the database.
    • The database gets two minutes to stop cleanly (stop_grace_period in production.yml), instead of being killed after 10 seconds and replaying its log at the next start.
  • Monitoring with Sentry: traces from the browser to the database.
    • See where the backend spends its time in Sentry: traces of API requests include their database queries, and a share of the backend's processes are profiled (SENTRY_PROFILE_SESSION_SAMPLE_RATE). Celery workers report their errors and tasks too (Monitoring with Sentry).
    • See the web app's page loads, web vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) and the API requests they make in the same Sentry trace as the backend's work, with readable stack traces: set SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_ORG, SENTRY_PROJECT and SENTRY_URL when you build the frontend image to upload its source maps, that are then no longer served.
    • Sentry is enabled by SENTRY_DSN alone (it also required FLASK_ENV=production), tags events with SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT and the release, traces 20% of requests by default (SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE), and checks the Sentry server's certificate (CA_CERT_URL build argument or SENTRY_CA_CERTS). Users are identified by their username only, tokens are filtered out, and SENTRY_FRONTEND_DSN sends the web app's events to their own project.
  • API: for scripts, agents and the image viewer.
    • Get the numbers of the Summary and Metrics Diff views from scripts and agents, with the experimental /api/v1/commit/<sha>/compare: each metric's median vs a reference, each run vs its reference run, and how many runs failed. See Quality gate.
    • API: page through /api/v1/commits with limit and offset (the X-Has-More header tells if there are more) and search them with q, find branches with /api/v1/project/branches?q=..., and get a much smaller list of projects with /api/v1/projects?summary=true (lists of commits). Without these parameters, they answer as before.
    • The API reads the values of a region of an image, for the image viewer's pixel values: GET /api/v1/output/image/pixels with image_url, x, y, w and h (up to 256×256 pixels), as JSON, or as binary with format=binary (their type and shape in the X-Pixels-Dtype and X-Pixels-Shape headers). What the image's reader says of the sensor (CFA pattern and cell size, bit depth, black level) comes along in sensor, or the X-Pixels-Sensor header: readers with other field names can be added in backend/backend/sensor.py.
    • The API finding where two images differ (POST /api/v1/output/image/diff) returns regions as x, y, w, h with the peak's value (comparable across images) and its fraction of the largest (diff), instead of a center and radius. It takes the reference's file name as path_ref, answers 404 for a missing file and 400 for images of different sizes, and keeps its results.
    • Images whose pixel values users read are decoded once and kept on disk, up to QABOARD_IMAGE_CACHE_GB (20 GB by default, the least recently used are removed), in QABOARD_IMAGE_CACHE_DIR. See the server's settings.
    • The server reads videos with FFmpeg (PyAV, in the backend's image), for the video viewer: what's in them (GET /api/v1/output/video/info), the decoded values of a frame's pixels (GET /api/v1/output/video/pixels, like images' with a frame), and where two videos differ, frame by frame (POST /api/v1/output/video/diff). Results are kept for a month in videos/, in QABOARD_IMAGE_CACHE_DIR.
  • Before running from a commit's artifacts, the server checks they are usable (the subproject's qaboard.yaml, the files in the manifests), and never runs from an incomplete folder.
  • The automated cleanup deletes artifacts again when storage.garbage.artifacts.delete is set: it was skipping every commit. Deleting a subproject's artifacts keeps the files the other subprojects of the commit still use.
  • qaboard_clean --dryrun no longer marks outputs as deleted in the database, and prints a summary of what was (or would be) deleted.

Documentation​

Getting started​

  • Run QA-Board on your computer with the new quickstart: one Docker Compose file, or a kind cluster and the Helm chart, with demo projects to look at, then results from an example project.
  • Put your project on QA-Board step by step with the tutorial: pick your server, code hosting, CI and runners once at the top, and every step shows the instructions for your stack. Links keep your choices (e.g. ?server=k8s&ci=gitlab-ci).
  • See what QA-Board is for in your first review and in one use case per demo project of a fictional robotics company, starting with image quality. New: odometry and mapping for robotics, evaluating an LLM agent, and tests and coverage over time: unit test suites from any runner that writes JUnit XML, with flaky and deleted tests caught. The key concepts fit in one page.
  • Find the quickstart, the review loop, each viewer (videos and 3D included) and what's coming next on the website's new home page. Links to the docs shared in chats show a card with a glimpse of the web app.

User guide​

  • New user guide for people who use the web app every day.
  • See the web app in screenshots and clips of the demo projects on every page of the user guide, each image viewer tool included, and next to the settings that produce them in the project integration docs, like Visualizations.
  • Release notes going back to 2017, on the website and in the app.
  • Start from the user guide's front door: the few words you need, a map of the commit page, and one page per task, like reading metrics, new and reference, milestones, choosing the tests to run and logs and failed runs.
  • Learn each viewer on its own page: images and videos, each with a typical review and all its shortcuts, and plots, flame graphs, 3D and more.
  • Read user guide pages that start with the most common task, with the details in collapsed sections.

Project integration and server docs​

  • Many pages updated to match the code, and features that were never documented: GitHub webhooks, API tokens, batch options, bit-accuracy manifests, auto-optimization...
  • The project setup and CI pages cover GitHub and GitLab equally (CI integration), and admins get a new git hosts page.
  • Set up single sign-on and decide who gets an account with the new sign-in and single sign-on page.
  • Find the server docs in one place, written for any site: starting a server, deployments and rollbacks with deploy.py, Kubernetes, host maintenance, backups and troubleshooting.
  • Write your own file viewer: see Viewers and file formats.
  • Start with how a project integrates QA-Board: the steps from installing qa to running in CI, and what you get after each.
  • Find what each viewer reads, and its options, on the new Viewers and file formats page, and matrices, YAML anchors and metadata filters on advanced batches.
  • Read the setup, batch, CI, tuning and recipe pages with examples from the demo projects, shown from their files so they stay up to date.
  • See where QA-Board is going on the new roadmap: its principles, and for each theme what's shipped, experimental, next or still being explored.

The website​

  • Follow old links to pages that moved or were removed: they redirect to the closest page.
  • The docs show a placeholder that describes a screenshot or clip when your browser can't load it, instead of a broken image.

Performance​

Several references​

  • Switch between stacked references without waiting: once the page is idle, the next and previous references load in the background (except very big ones), and the others load without their runs, enough for their tabs to show their branch and message.

Commit pages with 1000 runs​

  • Type in the filter box of a commit page without the page freezing: the results update in half a second, instead of after 7 seconds of a frozen page. Sorting runs, and matching them with their reference, no longer freeze the page either.
  • Open the Metrics Table in a third of a second instead of 7 seconds, with a fraction of the memory (40 MB instead of 640 MB): big tables only render the rows on screen.
  • Open the Visualizations twice as fast: cards download their files as they scroll into view, and files shared by several cards or viewers are downloaded once. Batches with more than 300 runs show more cards as you scroll, or all of them with "show all".
  • Commit pages load in 0.6 s instead of 1 s.
  • Switch between references twice as fast, without the page freezing: the Summary shows the new reference's numbers at once, then updates its plots one after the other. Pages with many plots no longer freeze while they draw.
  • Open tuning batches faster: runs that have an exact match in the reference no longer go through a name-similarity search.

Everywhere in the web app​

  • Start the web app faster: it downloads a quarter less JavaScript on first load (date picker, error reporting and number formatting load only when needed), and servers send precompressed files.
  • Come back to a page you already visited, or reload, and it shows up at once from your browser's cache, then refreshes in the background. Commits with running outputs keep updating.
  • Open commits sooner: hovering a commit in a list starts loading its page, and a project's commits no longer wait for its configuration.
  • Hover the History plot and image-heavy pages more smoothly: the page updates once you pause on a commit, and image viewers you've left no longer keep redrawing in the background.

Logs​

  • Scroll through hundreds of runs in the Logs view without slowdowns.
  • Open very long logs (tens of thousands of lines) several times faster, and search them without the page freezing for seconds.
  • See the diff of big text files (logs, configurations...) with the reference sooner: the editor loads while the files download, instead of after.

Images​

  • Find where images differ faster: on a 12 MP image in under a second instead of 4 to 8 seconds, on a 96 MP image in 4 to 5 seconds instead of 6 to 18 (under a second for another way to compare), and at once the next time. Differences of a few pixels in large images are no longer missed.
  • Read the values of pixels in large 16-bit or raw images without waiting: the image viewer loads them by tiles of 64×64 pixels and keeps them, the server sends them as binary, decodes each image once even when many users open it at the same time, and no longer decodes images again after 20 others.

Fixes​

Across the web app​

  • The whole web app says Sign in and Sign out: the sidebar, the viewers and the file browser used different words.
  • The cheat sheet (?) lists the viewers' real shortcuts: h starts a blind test, < and > change a video's speed, and the run filter's example fail keeps the failed runs. The image viewer's own list includes full screen (f).
  • The batch menu says Move the filtered runs to another batch when you filter runs, instead of the other way around.
  • The automated tuning example names the solver's acq_func option correctly.
  • Copying the path of an output, batch or commit directory gives the right path when folder names contain characters like #, and the confirmation shows the copied path.
  • Notifications show at the bottom of the window again, instead of at the bottom of the page's first screen where they were out of sight once you scrolled down.
  • Move on quickly from the sidebar's Integrations and Milestones menus: they close once the mouse leaves them, instead of staying up to 3 seconds over the page.
  • Links to the LSF docs and to the getting-started page work again, and the retired chat link now points to your server's support page (by default, QA-Board's GitHub issues).

Commit page​

  • Run cards draw the visualizations of projects that still list them under their old name, outputs.detailed_views, instead of empty cards under the View options' switches.
  • The controls panel shows the sort actually used, the project's default metric, instead of Name, and Output Files no longer shows an empty visualization filter.
  • Run cards grow to fit a plot wider than their configured width (outputs.style.width), instead of the plot spilling out of the card.
  • Run cards with a configured width (outputs.style.width) get narrower when the page is, e.g. when the View options are open, instead of going under them and hiding the image viewer's zoom and settings.
  • Visualization cards line up from the left, instead of being pushed to the edges of the page.
  • The Tuning Analysis view's efficient frontier colors points by nested tuning parameters (like denoise.strength) instead of drawing black dots.
  • Dynamic options no longer show an empty card when a run doesn't have the selected value, sort numbers as numbers (2 before 10), and no longer split into options like frame_1234 that control nothing. Whether an option is linked is no longer remembered across projects.
  • A run's card in full screen has a button to leave it, and scrolls when it's taller than the screen, instead of its content sticking to the screen's edges.
  • Hiding a visualization shown by default takes one click instead of two.
  • The reference commit's refresh button works again: it was disabled once the commit had loaded.
  • The error page shows the error as text, instead of inserting it in the page as HTML.
  • Artifacts & Configs shows the artifacts again when the commit loads after the view, instead of "Could not find" them.

Metrics and tables​

  • A run is compared with the reference run of the same platform: when the reference batch had the same input and configuration on two platforms, the other platform's run was picked.
  • The Improvement report showed "=" for metrics that changed, and badges for those that didn't.
  • The Summary's change in % has the right sign for metrics with negative values, and runs that return no value (null) for a metric no longer count as 0 in its median.
  • The Summary only warns that it mixes runs with different parameters when the runs it aggregates really have different parameters: filter the runs to compare one configuration.
  • In the Metrics Table, the New and Ref headers stay over their columns when a filter leaves out every run that has some metric, and metrics without a target show just their unit, like [s].
  • Removing a metric from a table's metric picker no longer also drops the selected metrics that the current batch doesn't have.
  • The Summary's box plots on a log scale show a few round ticks, instead of labels that overlapped.
  • Output Files tags runs Bit-accurate when their output files match the reference's: like qa check-bit-accuracy, it only checks the files that match bit_accuracy.patterns in qaboard.yaml (all files by default, except logs, run.json and metrics.json). The other files are still listed when they differ, greyed and tagged "not checked". See bit-accuracy tests.

Image viewer​

  • In the image viewer, changing a Dynamic Option (e.g. a slider over your pipeline's stages) keeps the zoom and the selected ROI, for the new and reference images, instead of zooming out to the whole image, most often when the reference's image showed up. Images with another aspect ratio fit the selected ROI again.
  • The regions where images differ most (formerly Auto ROIs) are centered on the differences, instead of starting at them.
  • Images show in the image viewer on servers that don't set QABOARD_IMAGE_SERVERS: the default is now Cantaloupe's /iiif/2/ endpoint, instead of a /iiif URL that Cantaloupe couldn't answer.
  • JPEG images show in the image viewer again, instead of an "Image Download Error": the image server only sent them as JPEG tiles, and the viewer asks for PNG ones. They now come as PNG tiles, with the exact pixel values for the pixel tooltip and the diff. Update the cantaloupe image to get the fix.
  • The image viewer's Auto ROIs finds regions again, instead of failing with an error.
  • The image viewer's ROI thumbnails show the image the viewer shows: they no longer break for runs that save a TIFF instead of a PNG, or for images served by another image server (QABOARD_IMAGE_SERVERS).
  • ROIs set on inputs of another size than the output images are placed right on non-square images, in the thumbnails and when you zoom on them.
  • In the image viewer, selecting a region (the selection button, or c) draws it again and shows its histograms, instead of panning the image.
  • The image viewer's diff threshold slider no longer jumps to its maximum and gets stuck: it moves step by step after you turn the diff on.

Videos, plots and other viewers​

  • Point clouds take the colors and names of what you compare, like the other viewers: blue for new, the reference's color and its name, e.g. a milestone's, instead of orange for new and blue for the reference.
  • In the video viewer, n and N go to the frames that differ more than the frames around them. On videos where every frame differs, like with a new denoiser, they no longer only go back to the first frame.
  • Text diffs stay side by side in narrow run cards, as the Side-by-side button says, and inline diffs are tall enough to show every changed line.
  • Playing or pausing a video that has no reference no longer raises errors ("pause is not a function").
  • Videos your browser can't play (e.g. HEVC) say so, with the command to convert them, instead of staying black. Animated .webp and .gif files now show, side by side with the reference's, instead of a black box or their bytes as text.
  • In point clouds, WASD moves while the key is pressed, not after it's released.
  • Plots saved with side_by_side: false draw the reference run's traces on the same axes, instead of nothing when a figure has several traces. Traces keep their own dash style.
  • Differential flame graphs are colored by what changed: red for frames that take more time than in the reference, blue for less, orange for new ones. The colors no longer exaggerate changes near the root.
  • The SLAM and tuning plots no longer have Plotly's "Send to Cloud" button, so their data can't be uploaded to Plotly's public cloud.
  • Text viewers set to show only differences hide identical files, and videos play without a reference.
  • Text files in a run's output files show again when the reference run doesn't have them, and their diff with the reference no longer breaks when you press t to swap the sides.
  • HTML outputs (like a run's report) show their images and links, which are relative to their own folder, and their styles no longer change the rest of the page: they show in a frame, without running scripts.

Commits, branches and history​

  • Clicking a run's name opens its History from 3 days before the commit, so you see the commits before it without picking dates.
  • Projects without a qaboard.yaml use master as their reference branch in the web app, like the server and qa, instead of develop.
  • Reloading a page, opening a shared link or using the back button shows what the URL says: the selected commits, batches and filters could disagree with it.
  • The back button takes you back in one click after following links inside QA-Board: some links added two entries to the browser's history.
  • The chart above a branch's commits shows the branch's metrics, the median or average over each commit's runs, instead of staying empty. Each commit row also shows the median and average of the default metric over its CI runs.
  • History's "Performance over time" chart shows your project's metrics again, instead of asking you to define them.
  • The History page's per-test tables show their metric columns again, in tabs named "Metrics Table" and "Metrics Diff" like on commit pages.
  • On the History page, picking metrics updates the metrics distribution too.
  • Selecting a milestone from qaboard.yaml selects the latest commit of its branch.
  • The batch selector no longer jumps back to the top while you scroll it, and its keyboard navigation works again. It now opens on the selected batch, marked with a check.
  • Switching to a branch you had opened in a previous visit no longer crashes the commits list ("setHours is not a function").
  • Commit pages and the branch list no longer break when results were sent without a branch.
  • The projects list shows the description from qaboard.yaml (project.description) for projects that aren't on GitHub or GitLab too.
  • The chart above a branch's commits leaves out the commits that don't have the metric, instead of drawing gaps in its line.
  • Typing a commit id in the commits list's search and pressing Enter no longer leaves "[object Object]" in the search box.
  • Editing your own shared milestone no longer asks whether to overwrite it.

Runs, batches and tuning​

  • Compute times are right in run menus: 90 seconds said "2min30s".
  • Run qa --share batch with an edited qaboard.yaml to see its new visualizations and metrics on that batch, while the commit's other batches, CI included, keep the commit's. Each qa batch used to replace the commit's qaboard.yaml for all its batches.
  • The automated tuning form's feedback link goes to your server's support page, and is left out when the server has none.
  • Redoing runs from QA-Board respects the batch's concurrency, and uses the runner the runs were started with (e.g. Dask) and its settings. QA-Board used to start each run with its own qa batch, so they all ran at once, with the default runner.
  • Runs that start again (redo, qa batch...) no longer show as failed, and count as failed, until they finish: their status is reset when they are pending or running.
  • Finished runs whose metrics don't include is_failed count as successful, instead of neither successful nor failed.
  • A stuck run's "Mark as Finished" action is now labelled "Mark as Failed", which is what it does.
  • Moving runs to another batch closes the dialog, and saving a milestone no longer risks losing it.
  • The tuning form shows a readable error instead of the server's raw response.
  • The tuning form remembers the "Overwrite" option, and setting the number of iterations no longer crashes.
  • Run Tests / Tuning runs as you when you open it from a link: it no longer asks for a user it can't let you type, with Send disabled.
  • The Tuning Analysis view plots each iteration's metrics (those in the objective) next to the objective, for tunings run from now on: qa optimize used to get no metrics from the server.
  • Projects whose inputs are inside the project (a relative inputs.database, like inputs) see their tests in the Run Tests / Tuning form and in Available Tests: they are looked for in the commit's artifacts, where the runs started from QA-Board run, instead of in a folder of the server. In monorepos, from the root qaboard.yaml's folder, like qa does.
  • Run Tests / Tuning and Available Tests find the inputs of projects whose inputs.database uses {project} or {subproject} (e.g. /datasets/{project.name}), instead of looking for them from /.
  • When several of a commit's batch files define the same batch, Run Tests / Tuning and Available Tests use the last one, like qa batch, instead of the first.
  • Batches started from Run Tests / Tuning run like qa batch on your computer: they use the defaults set at the top of their batch file (database, configurations, platform), and when several files define a batch, the last one replaces it instead of being merged into it. QA-Board used to run a merged copy of the batch files that dropped these defaults; it now runs copies of each file, saved next to the logs.
  • Listing a batch's tests no longer fails for commits that QA-Board saw before qa sent their qaboard.yaml (e.g. opened by branch name): it uses the project's, and the commit gets its own the next time qa runs on it.
  • Run Tests / Tuning lists the tests of batches whose name contains +, & or #.
  • When a batch has an input it can't use, like an empty - or a number, qa batch says which batch, in which file and at which line, instead of "Could not understand the inputs in the batch" followed by all its inputs. Available Tests and Run Tests / Tuning show the same error.
  • Stopping a batch whose runs can't be stopped reports the error instead of failing.
  • The tuning form no longer asks for an Android device, which runs never received.
  • qa batch --runner=local (or any --runner) uses the batch's and the input type's settings for that runner, e.g. its local concurrency and timeout, also when the project's default runner is another one, like LSF.

CLI​

  • Give a batch its own concurrency (under local:, lsf: or dask:) or local timeout: its runs now use it instead of the command's. Command-line options like --local-concurrency still win, even when they equal the value in qaboard.yaml.
  • Runs over their local timeout fail, and qa batch kills what they started and goes on with the other runs, instead of stopping with a TimeoutError and leaving them pending.
  • Inputs with their own settings can set their platform:, and no longer make qa batch fail with KeyError: 'platform' in batches that set one.
  • qa batch '*' runs your batches only, instead of also running every input as a batch named aliases.
  • qa batch --action-on-existing assert-exists leaves the runs that already succeeded as they are, instead of failing them with a command that doesn't exist.
  • qa wait exits with an error when the run it waited for failed, so qa wait ... || ... works.
  • qa optimize works without --checkpoint, instead of failing with a TypeError.
  • qa check-bit-accuracy --reference-platform finds the reference's runs on the other platform when runs have configurations, instead of saying there is no reference.
  • qa tells you to run qa init, not qatools init, when it can't find qaboard.yaml, and qa batch --help says that --local-concurrency -1 runs one run per CPU.
  • With LSF job arrays and the Dask runner, qa run no longer deletes the log file its output goes to: errors are no longer lost.
  • Runs on Dask workers are headless, like with LSF: they use matplotlib's agg backend and no DISPLAY, instead of opening X11 connections back to the display of whoever started the batch.
  • Runs started from a git worktree checkout are saved under their commit, instead of their branch name. Submodules with a relative .git pointer also work.
  • On Windows, qa works in a git worktree whose .git pointer holds an absolute Linux path: it is translated with the site's path mappings (QABOARD_PATH_MAPPINGS).
  • qa starts even when the git HEAD cannot be read, e.g. an unresolvable worktree pointer: it warns and continues with <local:user> commit placeholders instead of crashing at startup.
  • On Windows, qa batch finds existing results for projects whose name contains a "/", instead of failing with "could not find any data on commit ID": --action-on-existing works there.
  • qa optimize works with recent versions of scikit-optimize, instead of failing with "cannot import name 'Integer'".
  • qa optimize no longer fails at the end when matplotlib isn't installed: it only skips its convergence plot.
  • qa batch --tuning-search runs a grid search when the JSON doesn't say search_type, as the docs show, instead of failing with KeyError: 'search_type'.
  • qa no longer warns that it doesn't know where your server is when you set QABOARD_URL=http://localhost:5151.
  • qa no longer prints a git error when the commit it runs on isn't in the local clone (e.g. shallow CI clones): it only did without the commit's details. QA_VERBOSE=1 still shows it.
  • With Python 3.12 and later, qa no longer prints a SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence when it starts.
  • qa batch accepts a single input written as text (inputs: a.jpg), and says that a batch written as a list (my-batch: [a, b]) must be a mapping with inputs:, also in the web app (the server used to call exit() there).
  • qa get works with Python 3.13: it said "Could not find" for every variable.
  • bit_accuracy.on_reference_failed_ci: compare-first-parent goes back up to bit_accuracy.max_parents_depth parents, instead of two at most.
  • bit_accuracy.failed_ci_job_name works again: qa check-bit-accuracy only looks at that job (<job> <subproject> in subprojects).
  • qa check-bit-accuracy counts skipped CI jobs as successful, instead of waiting for them.
  • Windows test vectors no longer fail bit-accuracy on hex outputs whose end-of-lines differ.

Server and administration​

  • LDAP accounts get their email from QABOARD_LDAP_ATTRIBUTE_EMAIL when it isn't mail: only mail was read.
  • Show the demo projects' latest commits in the quickstart's commit list: the demo data's dates, and its files' modification times, move to when QA-Board first starts, instead of keeping the day the demo data was made (quickstart).
  • The project's settings (metrics, visualizations, storage...) are no longer replaced by those of whichever branch got new results last: they come from the reference branch (project.reference_branch in qaboard.yaml), or from the project's first results.
  • nginx starts on hosts without IPv6, instead of failing on its listen [::]:80 line.
  • Repositories whose clone is broken are cloned again, instead of failing until an admin deletes them. The broken clone is only replaced once the new clone succeeded.
  • Tag pushes record the tag's whole name: its first character was cut.
  • Pushes to repositories with files or folders whose name only looks like qaboard.yaml (for example an agent skill folder named qaboard-yaml) no longer fail: only files named exactly qaboard.yaml or qatools.yaml define projects.
  • Jenkins integrations show the status of the builds they trigger when Jenkins' own URL uses another hostname than the integration's build_url (for example a full domain name): checking them failed with a 403 because no credentials matched that hostname in JENKINS_AUTH.
  • Jenkins integrations trigger jobs that have no parameters, and when Jenkins refuses a build the error says why (HTTP status, Jenkins' message, a hint about JENKINS_AUTH or build_url) instead of showing a whole HTML page about a missing location header.
  • Servers outside SIRC no longer show avatars from SIRC's directory for GitLab users without one: set QABOARD_AVATAR_URL to use your own (environment variables).
  • Backend workers no longer risk crashing, or losing Sentry events, when Sentry is enabled: Sentry starts in each uWSGI worker, and uwsgi.ini sets py-call-uwsgi-fork-hooks, as Sentry's SDK requires. Keep it if you use your own uwsgi.ini.
  • The cleanup also deletes commits that never had runs, and uses each project's own storage.garbage settings instead of the first project's.
  • storage.garbage.artifacts.keep now works with artifact group names, and also accepts folders and globs.
  • Commits whose artifacts were only partly restored are no longer marked as usable.
  • qaboard_clean --dryrun no longer deletes the folders of runs without a manifest, or with a corrupted one.

Security and data safety​

  • Requiring sign-in now blocks anonymous requests to the API itself, not only the web app's pages.
  • API tokens are no longer stored in clear, and a token in a URL (?token=) is only accepted to read. Requests made with a token no longer open a session cookie.
  • Session cookies are HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, and Secure when QABOARD_URL is https. Changes made with cookies must come from QA-Board's own pages.
  • Signing in with SAML only sends you back to QA-Board's own pages (open redirect), and lands on the home page instead of an empty error page when there's nowhere to go back to.
  • Logging in no longer sends everything the directory knows about you to the browser.
  • Reading the values of an image's or a video's pixels, what's in a video, and finding where images or videos differ now require a login, and only read files in the storage (QABOARD_STORAGE_ROOTS) that you're allowed to see. Signed out, the viewers show the displayed values and say to sign in for the rest. These endpoints could read images anywhere on the server, without a login.
  • The unused PDF report of the regions where images differ (/api/v1/output/diff/report) is removed: it could write files anywhere on the server, without a login.
  • Marking a run as failed or deleting it now requires a login.
  • On servers that restrict projects to some users, only users allowed on a project can stop, rename, move or delete its batches, delete a commit's results, save its artifacts, or change its milestones. Exporting runs also checks you can access the reference's project.
  • QABOARD_LOGIN_RESTRICTED=false (or 0) turns project restrictions off, as you would expect: any non-empty value used to turn them on.
  • Deleting results no longer deletes the contents of folders that they link to.
  • When a restricted project saves its results in a folder per user (e.g. /algo/outputs/{user}), the project's files are now restricted in every user's folder, not only in the server's.
  • The API qa uses to update batches no longer lets anyone without a login delete runs. qa optimize still replaces its previous best iteration's runs, and only those.
  • When qa fails to update QA-Board, its warning no longer prints your API token (QA_TOKEN).
  • When signing up with a user name or email that is already used, the server answers "already taken" instead of an error that included the password's hash, and no longer writes the password to its logs.
  • Logging in with an empty password is refused, and LDAP logins escape the user name.
  • The server only deletes the git clones it made: it refuses repository paths inside a clone, or that hold other clones.

entry.content:
Cap how many runs of a batch use the LSF cluster at the same time, or run batches of short runs on a pool of Dask workers. The server is easier to deploy from scratch, and re-running outputs or tuning on LSF goes through the configured LSF bridge.

Project integration

Limit batch concurrency on LSF

Set runners.lsf.concurrency in qaboard.yaml, or use qa batch --lsf-concurrency 20, so a batch never has more than 20 LSF jobs running at once and doesn't flood the cluster. The default, 0, keeps the previous behavior: no limit.

Learn more →
Project integration

Dask runner

With qa batch --runner dask, a batch's runs execute on a few long-lived Dask workers started as LSF jobs, with a bounded number of runs in flight. It avoids paying LSF's scheduling overhead for each of many short runs. Install it with pip install "qaboard[dask]".

Learn more →

CLI and project setup​

  • By default the LSF concurrency limit uses an LSF job array with a slot limit: a new run starts as soon as one ends. Set runners.lsf.concurrency_strategy: waves to send runs in groups that each wait for the previous group to end, if job arrays don't work for you.
  • The Dask runner is configured under runners.dask in qaboard.yaml: concurrency (or --dask-concurrency), the worker jobs' cluster size and memory, and scheduler_address to use a Dask cluster you already run.
  • With --no-wait, the Dask runner sends a small "driver" LSF job that runs the batch, with its own LSF options (runners.dask.driver), and qa batch returns right away.
  • Dask workers' and the driver's logs are saved in the batch directory, under dask/, and each run's output directory gets a log.dask.txt. Stopping a batch from QA-Board also stops its Dask workers.
  • qa save-artifacts and other commands no longer crash with "'NoneType' object is not iterable" in legacy projects whose configuration defines no inputs.

Server and administration​

  • "Redo" actions on a batch (deleted, failed or all outputs) and tuning batches sent to LSF from the web app now go through the backend's QA_RUNNERS_LSF_BRIDGE, which supports the {user} and {bsub_command} placeholders, instead of a hardcoded SSH host. Set it to use these features with LSF (see LSF bridges).
  • The Flower dashboard for Celery now runs from the backend image: there is no separate Flower image to build anymore.
  • The documentation site's image now builds with Docusaurus 3.10.
  • The SIRC deployment's files, including .env.sirc.example, now all live under deployments/sirc/.

Documentation​

  • New Dask integration page. The CLI docs now list the batch runners (local, LSF, Dask, Celery) and how to limit their concurrency, and the LSF page documents --lsf-concurrency.

Fixes​

  • Fixed results uploads failing (HTTP 500 on every new output) on servers whose database was created from scratch rather than migrated from an older version.
  • The database container now starts on a fresh, empty volume: its custom configuration is applied only once the database is initialized.
  • Fixed Docker builds that download a CA certificate (CA_CERT_URL) failing when the certificate file already existed.

Notes​

  • The LSF concurrency limit and the Dask runner are in qaboard 1.1, released in October.

entry.title: 2026-q2
entry.summary: The image viewer shows TIFF versions of PNG outputs when they exist and compares outputs saved in different formats. Jenkins build statuses update live and survive page refreshes, and shared milestones now have owners and can be filtered by person.
entry.content:
The image viewer shows TIFF versions of PNG outputs when they exist and compares outputs saved in different formats. Jenkins build statuses update live and survive page refreshes, and shared milestones now have owners and can be filtered by person.

Users

TIFF versions of images

When an output has both image.png and image.tiff, the image viewer shows the TIFF. When comparing to a reference saved in another format, each side falls back to the file it has: TIFF, PNG or the older BMP.

Learn more →
Users

Live Jenkins build status

After you trigger a Jenkins build from the commit page, its status tag now updates on its own (queued, running, then the result), and it is still there when you refresh the page or come back to the commit in the same browser.

Learn more →
Users

Milestone owners

Shared milestones remember who created them and the commit's author. Filter milestones by their names, and only a milestone's owners can edit or delete it.

Learn more →

Web app​

  • Pixel values shown when you hover an image are now read from the file actually displayed (the TIFF when it is used), and always match the pixel under the cursor. They could be off by one pixel before, especially at the image's edges.
  • In the "Output Files" view, opening a TIFF or a PNG also falls back to the other format on the side (new or reference) that doesn't have it.
  • Build status icons are clearer: a clock while a build is queued or pending, a spinning icon while it runs, and a pause icon only for blocked or stuck builds.
  • Integration links inside sub-menus are now checked too, so broken links show up there like in top-level menus.
  • Saving, editing or deleting a shared milestone now requires being logged in. Milestones saved before this change have no owner: any logged-in user can still edit them, and becomes an owner by doing so. Milestones show their commit's author as a tag.

Server and administration​

  • Added services/vips, a small Docker image with the libvips command line tools, to convert PNG outputs to TIFF.

Fixes​

  • The loading spinner of the image viewer now disappears once the images are loaded, including for the reference image and for images already in the browser's cache.
  • Jenkins builds triggered from the commit page are now polled for their status. Before, their status could stay stuck after the trigger.
  • Integrations with the same name in different menus no longer share their status.
  • When qa reports a commit the server can't find, the server answers with a clear error instead of crashing.

entry.summary: Synced zoom and pan in the image viewer stays smooth on pages with many images, and the server can track GitHub repositories. Every deployment now runs the same code: site-specific settings moved to compose overlays and to site packages for the qa CLI.
entry.content:
Synced zoom and pan in the image viewer stays smooth on pages with many images, and the server can track GitHub repositories. Every deployment now runs the same code: site-specific settings moved to compose overlays and to site packages for the qa CLI.

Users

Smoother synced zoom and pan

On pages with many images, zooming or panning one image no longer slows down the page: only the images on screen follow along, and the others catch up instantly when you scroll to them. Images that load late open at the current zoom and position.

Learn more →
Admins

GitHub repositories

Besides GitLab, the server can now follow projects hosted on GitHub or GitHub Enterprise: it receives push events on /webhook/github, clones the repositories with GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN and shows GitHub avatars. Commit statuses and GitHub Actions are not supported yet.

Learn more →
Admins

One codebase for every site

The base docker-compose.yml now has open-source defaults, and each site adds its own settings with an overlay in deployments/, for example deployments/sirc/sirc.yml. Copy deployments/example.yml to describe your own site.

Learn more →
Users

Site packages for the qa CLI

Install qaboard[sirc] to get your site's defaults (server URL, secrets location, internal dependencies) without setting environment variables. Environment variables still override them.

Learn more →

Web app​

  • The visualizations section of the commit page's controls panel shows up right away, instead of waiting for every output's file list to load.
  • Avatars from any git server now go through QA-Board, so they are no longer blocked as mixed content when QA-Board is served over HTTPS.

CLI and project setup​

  • Without QABOARD_HOST or a site package, qa now connects to http://localhost:5151, the default local server. It used to try an internal SIRC server. At SIRC, install qaboard[sirc] (see Client Installation).
  • Removed qaboard.on_vdi and qaboard.on_lsf, which detected SIRC hosts from the hostname: update project code that imports them. Site packages now provide site-specific settings.
  • An internal SIRC dependency is now installed only with qaboard[sirc], so pip install qaboard works outside SIRC.

Server and administration​

  • Deploy with your site's overlay on top of the base files, e.g. docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f production.yml -f deployments/sirc/sirc.yml up -d. Site-specific nginx configuration, volumes and services (fluentd, metabase...) moved to deployments/<site>/.
  • The Docker images build with no arguments by default. Behind a proxy, pass the PROXY_URL, CA_CERT_URL and NO_PROXY build args, and QABOARD_EXTRA to include a site package in the backend image.
  • Credentials for LDAP, Sentry and PostHog are read from a .env file instead of the compose files. .env.sirc.example lists the SIRC variables.
  • The web app now gets its settings from the server when it loads (image servers, login type, Sentry and PostHog keys, path mappings, docs URL), so changing them no longer requires rebuilding the web app image.
  • QABOARD_IMAGE_SERVERS picks the IIIF image server per file extension, e.g. one server for raw images and Cantaloupe for the rest.
  • QABOARD_PATH_MAPPINGS (a JSON list of Windows/Linux path pairs) replaces the hardcoded mappings used to convert paths between Windows shares and Linux.
  • QABOARD_TUNING_RUNNER chooses how tuning batches started from the web app run: local (default), celery or lsf. QABOARD_DEFAULT_USER sets the user that owns their outputs. See tuning from the web app.
  • GITLAB_HOST and GITLAB_ACCESS_TOKEN are no longer required to start the backend: without a token, repositories are cloned anonymously.
  • The backend now gives up after 20 seconds when the database is unreachable, instead of hanging silently.

Documentation​

  • The server and client installation docs describe the compose overlays and site packages. MIGRATION.md, at the root of the repository, lists the changes to make when upgrading an existing deployment.

Fixes​

  • Opening another page now always starts images at the default zoom, even when the previous page had images synced with the same key.
  • Fixed crashes of the backend when several people read pixel values on the same image at the same time. Its image cache, which had been turned off because of them, is back on, so pixel values show up faster.
  • The visualizations panel now resets when you switch to another commit or batch, keeps your show/hide choices when the project configuration reloads, and lists the options found in all output files (only the first 1000 files were used).

entry.summary: Image and text viewers no longer react to their keyboard shortcuts while you type or use Ctrl/Cmd shortcuts, and the storage quota link works again.
entry.content:
Image and text viewers no longer react to their keyboard shortcuts while you type or use Ctrl/Cmd shortcuts, and the storage quota link works again.

Server and administration​

  • Added a database index on outputs (idx_outputs_batch_user_storage) that speeds up the storage quota dashboard. New databases get it automatically; on an existing database, create it by hand.

Fixes​

  • The image and text viewers' keyboard shortcuts (e.g. t to toggle between new and reference) no longer fire while you type in a text area or an editable field, or when you press Ctrl, Cmd or Alt combinations such as Ctrl+C.
  • The "Quota" entry in the commit list's menu opens the current storage dashboard again. It pointed to a dashboard that was deleted.

entry.summary: A fix for triggering Jenkins builds from the web app.
entry.content:
A fix for triggering Jenkins builds from the web app.

Fixes​

  • Triggering a Jenkins build from the web app no longer fails with an error when Jenkins's response about the queued build can't be read.

entry.title: 2025-q4
entry.summary: Use -- to pass arguments to your own code with qa run, qa postprocess and qa batch, and save your custom batches in the web app with Ctrl-S. The backend image moved to Debian trixie and Python 3.13.
entry.content:
Use -- to pass arguments to your own code with qa run, qa postprocess and qa batch, and save your custom batches in the web app with Ctrl-S. The backend image moved to Debian trixie and Python 3.13.

Users

Forward arguments with --

Everything after -- on the command line is passed as-is to your code, for example qa batch my-batch -- --my-flag. Late qa options like qa batch my-batch --list keep working.

Learn more →
Users

Ctrl-S to save custom batches

In the web app's editor for custom batches, used by tuning experiments, press Ctrl-S (Cmd-S on macOS) to save your changes instead of clicking "Update Batches".

Learn more →

CLI and project setup​

  • QA_BATCH_FILTER_INPUT_REGEX now matches anywhere in the input path, and ignores a leading ^.

Server and administration​

  • The backend image is now based on Debian trixie with Python 3.13, which also brings fixes for the XML libraries used by SAML login.

Fixes​

  • On Windows, the CLI uses Git for Windows' ssh when it is installed to fix the permissions of outputs on network storage, since the built-in ssh can't read keys from network paths. Paths with spaces are quoted correctly.

entry.title: 2025-q3
entry.summary: Copy a run's configuration in one click, ready to paste in a tuning experiment, and qa batch accepts several batch names at once. Commit pages use less memory on the server.
entry.content:
Copy a run's configuration in one click, ready to paste in a tuning experiment, and qa batch accepts several batch names at once. Commit pages use less memory on the server.

Users

Copy configurations, also in tuning format

Hover a run's configuration tags to copy one item, the full configuration, or the full configuration in the format the tuning form expects.

Users

Paste parameters into the tuning form

When you paste key=value parameter lines into the tuning form's editor, including multi-line matrices, they are converted to the tuning format for you.

Learn more →
Users

Several batches in one qa batch

Run qa batch first-batch second-batch instead of repeating --batch for each one. Options that start with a dash after the batch names are still forwarded to qa run.

Learn more →

Web app​

  • The batch selector marks milestone batches with a star, and works better with the keyboard.
  • On commits with many outputs, the controls panel shows how many outputs it has read options from, with a "Refresh Options" button to update them all.
  • The "Delete All Runs" menu item says more clearly that it deletes the runs in all other projects for this commit.

CLI and project setup​

  • qa batch fails with a clear error when a batch in batches.yaml is not a mapping (with inputs, configurations...), and warns about batches with an empty definition.
  • Set QA_BATCH_FILTER_INPUT_REGEX to only run the inputs of a batch whose path matches a regular expression.

Server and administration​

  • Commit pages use less memory on the server, and a commit that is missing from the database returns a clean 404.
  • The nginx image builds again: it now uses the Debian archive since Debian Buster reached its end of life.
  • The backend image builds its XML libraries from source to avoid library version mismatches. If SAML support can't load, the backend now starts anyway and logs a warning.
  • For contributors, development.yml runs the backend with uv run and as your own user.

Documentation​

  • The batches page uses the new qa batch first-batch second-batch syntax.

Fixes​

  • Fixed "Copy reference image to the clipboard", which copied the new image instead of the reference.
  • Fixed the size of the current region of interest in the image viewer.

entry.summary: The commit page has a new controls panel to pick visualizations, metrics and sorting, and options like the frame to show can now be synced across all outputs or set per output. Input types can have their own runner settings.
entry.content:
The commit page has a new controls panel to pick visualizations, metrics and sorting, and options like the frame to show can now be synced across all outputs or set per output. Input types can have their own runner settings.

Users

A controls panel on the commit page

A panel on the right side of the commit page gathers the viewer controls: which visualizations to show, with a filter box, the image diff toggle, sorting and the metrics to display. Collapse it with its arrow button when you need the room.

Learn more →
Users

Synced or per-output visualization options

Options that come from visualization paths, like :frame, default to synced: one control in the panel drives every output. Unsync an option to pick its value separately in each output card.

Learn more →
Project integration

Runner settings per input type

Input types in qaboard.yaml can now have their own runner settings under runners, for instance a different LSF queue for each type of input. Settings in a batch still win, and flags you pass to qa batch win over both.

Learn more →
Users

Searchable batch selector

The batch selector in the commit navbar is now a search box. Find a batch by name, by the user who launched it, or with words like failed, running or tuning.

Web app​

  • The image viewer's filters have a new panel with value displays, a reset button and a new Sharpen filter, next to Brightness, Contrast and Gamma.
  • In the bit-accuracy viewer, hover a file's size to download the new or the reference version of the file.
  • The filter box of the controls panel also filters the list of metrics.
  • Redesigned sidebar, with a user menu that shows who you are logged in as and lets you sign out.
  • You can search the sidebar's list of integrations, and menus keep their state when you close and reopen them.

CLI and project setup​

  • Runner settings are merged in this order, each winning over the previous: the runners section of qaboard.yaml, the input type's runners, the batch's runner settings, then the flags you pass explicitly to qa batch such as --lsf-queue or --local-concurrency.
  • --local-timeout and runners.local.timeout now set the timeout of local runs, not only QA_BATCH_TIMEOUT.
  • Removed qa batch --lsf-fast-queue: LSF jobs always use the regular queue.

Documentation​

  • The inputs page shows how to set runner settings per input type.

Fixes​

  • Fixed the CLI when it is embedded in a C++ program and has no command-line arguments.

entry.summary: qaboard 1.0.3 is packaged with a modern pyproject.toml, and the backend's dependencies are managed with uv. The image viewer stops flagging images whose pixels are identical as different.
entry.content:
qaboard v1.0.3

qaboard 1.0.3 is packaged with a modern pyproject.toml, and the backend's dependencies are managed with uv. The image viewer stops flagging images whose pixels are identical as different.

Users

Images compared by their pixels

When the outputs manifest has a hash of an image's pixel values, the image viewer uses it to decide whether the new and reference images are the same. Images that only differ in their metadata are no longer shown as changed.

Learn more →
Project integration

qaboard 1.0.3, built with pyproject.toml

The qaboard package is now defined in pyproject.toml instead of setup.py. Developers install it with uv sync --extra dev, and the backend's dependencies are locked with uv instead of poetry.

Learn more →

Web app​

  • Hover the colored dot of an automatic region of interest to see its diff value.

CLI and project setup​

  • The deprecated qatools package still ships for older scripts, and importing it now shows a deprecation warning: use qaboard instead.

Server and administration​

  • The backend image installs its dependencies with uv from backend/uv.lock.

entry.summary: You can find a run by its ID in the commit page's search box, and qa batch now stops before flooding QA-Board with more than 1,000 runs at once.
entry.content:
You can find a run by its ID in the commit page's search box, and qa batch now stops before flooding QA-Board with more than 1,000 runs at once.

Users

Search runs by ID

Type id:1234 in the commit page's filter box to show only the run with that ID, for instance when a colleague or a log gives you a run ID.

Project integration

A limit of 1,000 runs per qa batch

qa batch now fails when it would send more than 1,000 runs at once, which is usually a mistake in a batch definition. Set QA_BATCH_ALLOW_MANY_RUNS=1 when you really need more, or use qa --offline batch to run without reporting to QA-Board.

Learn more →

Server and administration​

  • The server updates the "latest results" time of commits and projects at most every few seconds, which avoids database lock contention when many runs report their results together.

Fixes​

  • qa run no longer crashes when writing the outputs manifest fails, it only warns.
  • Fixed qa optimize crashing when it sets QA_OPTIM_DIR.

entry.summary: You can copy the new, reference or diff image straight to the clipboard to paste it in a chat or a report. Admins get a backend tuned for heavy load, and production logs can go to a central collector.
entry.content:
You can copy the new, reference or diff image straight to the clipboard to paste it in a chat or a report. Admins get a backend tuned for heavy load, and production logs can go to a central collector.

Users

Copy images to the clipboard

The image viewer has a new Copy button. Click it to copy the new image, or hover it to copy the reference or the diff image instead. If your browser can't write images to the clipboard, the image is downloaded.

Learn more →
Admins

A backend tuned for heavy load

uWSGI workers now use threads, a larger request queue and longer timeouts, and are recycled when they use more than 4GB of memory. Fewer processes and smaller database connection pools keep PostgreSQL from running out of connections.

Web app​

  • The image viewer's zoom controls fade out faster, and the sidebar's menus close sooner after the mouse leaves them.

Server and administration​

  • Production deployments can forward the logs of the backend, database and redis containers to a fluentd log collector.
  • PostgreSQL now writes its logs to files and logs connections and disconnections, and accepts up to 200 connections.
  • Larger request headers are accepted (buffer-size 65535), and big uploads are buffered so they don't block a worker.

Fixes​

  • Fixed the diff image after the upgrade of the image viewer library.
  • HTML and Plotly viewers no longer stay blank when a file fails to load.
  • Fixed the visualization options (such as the frame selector) sometimes not appearing after the move to React 18.
  • Fixed a server error on some commit pages.

entry.summary: Commit pages load faster, especially for big batches and for commits that don't exist, and their errors now say what went wrong. The web app moved to React 18 and newer UI libraries.
entry.content:
Commit pages load faster, especially for big batches and for commits that don't exist, and their errors now say what went wrong. The web app moved to React 18 and newer UI libraries.

Users

Faster commit pages

The server now caches slow lookups like the list of users in redis, shared by all its workers, and the web app matches each run with its reference run much faster. Large commits open noticeably quicker.

Users

Clearer errors on the commit page

Hover the red "Error" tag in the commit navbar to see the server's message. It also tells you whether to check the commit and project you asked for, or to contact the QA-Board admins.

Web app​

  • Output cards keep a minimum height while they load, so scrolling a long list no longer starts loading too many images at once.
  • The reference image's label always shows the image size.
  • Upgraded to React 18, Redux 5 and recent Blueprint and Plotly versions.

Server and administration​

  • The backend now uses a redis service as a shared cache, with REDIS_HOST and REDIS_PORT (included in docker-compose.yml). Each worker warms the cache when it starts.
  • Asking for a full commit hash that has no results now fails right away with a 404, instead of a slow search.

Fixes​

  • Fixed an error when hovering an image while the diff image is hidden.
  • Fixed a server error when a run was reported without any extra data.
  • Fixed small display issues in the metrics, tables and tuning forms after the upgrade.

entry.summary: When you compare images, the diff image now shows the same crosshair as the new and reference images. The CLI can authenticate to the API with a QA_TOKEN environment variable.
entry.content:
When you compare images, the diff image now shows the same crosshair as the new and reference images. The CLI can authenticate to the API with a QA_TOKEN environment variable.

Users

Synced crosshair on the diff image

Hovering over the new or reference image now draws the crosshair at the same spot on the diff image too, so you can see where a difference is. It goes away when the mouse leaves the image.

Learn more →
Users

API token from QA_TOKEN

When the QA_TOKEN environment variable is set, the qa CLI and qaboard.api send it to the QA-Board API as a bearer token, which lets scripts and CI jobs call the API as a logged-in user.

Web app​

  • The crosshair stays in sync with the diff image while you zoom.

Fixes​

  • Fixed videos that never started playing when the browser had them in its cache.
  • Fixed the image viewer when an output has no reference to compare to.
  • qa check-bit-accuracy now looks for outputs on the platform you selected with --platform (or the batch's platform) instead of always the default platform.

entry.title: 2024-q4
entry.summary: Scripts can call the API with personal tokens, the video viewer keeps both videos in sync and shows the time of each, and runs remember which batch they came from. Image comparisons flag different sizes and failed tiles.
entry.content:
Scripts can call the API with personal tokens, the video viewer keeps both videos in sync and shows the time of each, and runs remember which batch they came from. Image comparisons flag different sizes and failed tiles.

Users

API tokens

Logged-in users can create a personal API token with a POST to /api/v1/user/token/, then authenticate scripts with an Authorization Bearer header or a token URL parameter.

Learn more →
Users

Synced video comparisons

The video viewer keeps the new and reference videos in sync, re-syncs when you pause, and shows the current time of each video and how far apart they are.

Users

Batch names on runs

Runs now record the name of the batch they were started from. It is shown in the run's menu, and you can filter runs by it.

Project integration

Metric descriptions

Metrics in metrics.yaml can have a description, shown in a tooltip on the metric's header.

Learn more →

Web app​

  • The image viewer shows both images' dimensions when they differ, and warns when some tiles fail to load.
  • Logs link directly to the LSF log when LSF killed the run.
  • Clearer error messages when tuning is not possible, and when an export folder is not writable or has locked-down permissions.
  • Style and help text improvements.

CLI and project setup​

  • exclude filters can match the input path relative to the database with rel_input_path.
  • QA_BATCH_TIMEOUT sets the timeout of local runs, and QA_BATCH_QUIET stops qa batch from printing each run's command and output directory.
  • qa check-bit-accuracy sets QA_BATCH, so batch-only metadata logic behaves as in qa batch.
  • When the server cannot report run statuses, qa batch warns and falls back to reading the output folders.
  • Fixed batch aliases, batches named matrix, and * input patterns.

Server and administration​

  • The local sign-up endpoint is enabled again, unless you set QABOARD_DISABLE_SIGNUP=True.
  • API tokens are stored in a new table (with a migration).
  • Batch summaries are counted in the database, using less memory, and file exports are faster.
  • Output folders created by the server are now writable by all users (umask 0), avoiding permission issues when runs write to them.

entry.title: 2024-q3
entry.summary: Admins can restrict access to specific projects or namespaces, exports let you choose how and where files go, and batches can be selected with wildcards. The qa CLI starts faster and the docs moved to Docusaurus 3.
entry.content:
Admins can restrict access to specific projects or namespaces, exports let you choose how and where files go, and batches can be selected with wildcards. The qa CLI starts faster and the docs moved to Docusaurus 3.

Admins

Per-project access control

The users restriction YAML has a new projects section to allow only some users into a project or a whole namespace. Sign-in rules move under a login key. Users now stay signed in for 180 days.

Learn more →
Users

Better file exports

Exporting results lets you choose between links and copies and set the destination folder on the shared storage. It warns about invalid file patterns, and reports errors and the number of exported files clearly.

Users

Wildcards for batches

qa batch 'batch-*' runs every matching batch, and wildcards also work in aliases and pipelines.

Learn more →
Users

Synced cursor in the image viewer

When comparing images, a cross shows on the other image where your mouse is, to compare the same pixels.

Web app​

  • The tuning form has a bigger editor, a nicer layout, and defaults to the linux platform.
  • The web app checks your session with the server instead of trusting what the browser remembers.
  • Errors about missing project permissions are shown on the commits list.
  • Better contrast, and tooltips are back.

CLI and project setup​

  • qa starts faster: imports are delayed, and it no longer makes a network request on every call to check for updates.
  • qa batch accepts several --tuning and --tuning-filepath options, merged together. String or list values go into a _config key whose items are appended to context.configs.
  • Batch YAML files can set default platform and configurations for all their batches, like database.
  • Batches without an inputs key match more inputs, including the database folder itself, and empty batch definitions now get a warning.
  • Fixed duplicated inputs in batches.
  • Fixed unstable output directories when redoing runs started from the web app.

Server and administration​

  • The docs explain how to develop with docker, and /docs on the server now leads to the docs.

Documentation​

  • The docs website moved to Docusaurus 3, and search results link correctly when the docs are served by the web app.
  • The user management page documents project access restrictions.

entry.title: 2024-q2
entry.summary: A quiet quarter: image comparisons fall back to BMP references when a PNG is missing, the image viewer shows when it is still loading, and tuning from the web app handles single quotes.
entry.content:
A quiet quarter: image comparisons fall back to BMP references when a PNG is missing, the image viewer shows when it is still loading, and tuning from the web app handles single quotes.

Users

Compare PNG outputs with older BMP references

When a run outputs a PNG image but the reference only has the same image as BMP, the file and image viewers now compare the two, and label which file is shown on each side.

Web app​

  • The image viewer shows a spinner until both images are fully loaded.
  • Plotly figures are shown side by side with the reference by default.
  • Integrations can use the reference commit as a variable (ref_commit).
  • Fixed the histogram when there is no reference, with clearer legends.

CLI and project setup​

  • Tuning parameters and configurations containing single quotes now work when tuning from the web app.
  • In batch matrices, values that are valid JSON (lists, objects...) are now parsed instead of being kept as strings.
  • GitLab commit statuses are retried a few times before giving up.
  • qa check-bit-accuracy stops early when nothing was compared.
  • Fixed --reference-label in some cases, and Windows UNC paths when computing output directories.

entry.title: 2024-q1
entry.summary: The integrations menu got nested items, per-batch configurations and more variables, and webhooks can open a page in response. The file viewer can filter on differing or matching files, and the web app moved to Blueprint 5.
entry.content:
The integrations menu got nested items, per-batch configurations and more variables, and webhooks can open a page in response. The file viewer can filter on differing or matching files, and the web app moved to Blueprint 5.

Project integration

Richer integrations menu

Integrations in qaboard.yaml can nest items with sub, appear directly in the sidebar with in_menu: false, and use variables for the selected batches, filters and logged-in user. Webhooks can return a url to show, and open it automatically with open: true.

Learn more →
Users

Filter files by comparison status

Admins can restrict sign-in to a list of users or groups, and projects spread over many repositories can share one templated configuration. Runs are matched with the reference more accurately, and output menus show compute times and the reference's directory.

Admins

Restrict who can sign in

With QABOARD_LOGIN_RESTRICTED=true and a YAML file set in QABOARD_LOGIN_RESTRICTED_YAML, only listed users can sign in, matched by user name, email or any attribute from the authentication provider. User details from the provider are now saved on each login.

Learn more →
Project integration

Shared configuration across repositories

project.name and project.url can use {root_path} and {project_path} placeholders, so many repositories can include the same qaboard.yaml. Submodules can set storage.artifacts.subproject to keep their artifacts organized.

Learn more →
Users

More accurate run matching

When comparing with a reference, runs are matched by input database and path, and still by input path alone when databases differ. Exports name files after the database when a batch mixes several.

Web app​

  • The output menu shows the run's compute time (for example "1h2min3s"), and offers to copy or open the reference's output directory, in titled sections.
  • The date range filter no longer needs both a start and an end date.
  • Deleting several batches skips milestones and batches that no longer exist.
  • Tuning warnings are shown as callouts, and more errors are displayed instead of failing silently.
  • Fixed state issues when the URL contains encoded characters.

CLI and project setup​

  • qa check-bit-accuracy compares RAW and HEX images by their attributes and pixel data, and warns and falls back to file hashes when attributes are missing.
  • Batches can change labels while their runs are ongoing.
  • Fixed submodule projects that used their parent's repository, and errors when LSF jobs had already finished.

Server and administration​

  • Git pushes no longer create commits ahead of time, which bloated the database of monorepos with hundreds of projects. Commits are recorded with their configuration and metrics when their first batch is posted.
  • New projects work whether their default branch is main or master.
  • Supports GitLab 16 sign-in.
  • Database JSON columns now use JSONB (with a migration).
  • The web app can report errors to Sentry with source maps and send product analytics to PostHog. Both are optional, enabled with build arguments.
  • pgAdmin is served under /pgadmin4/, and Flower can display pickled task data.
  • The docs and the dev setup now use docker compose instead of docker-compose.
  • Fixed race conditions in the image pixel API and when creating inputs, and errors when deleting the same run twice.

Documentation​

  • New user management page.
  • Expanded monorepo and multi-repo docs, input types in inputs, and how to debug runs.

entry.title: 2023-q3
entry.summary: QA-Board servers can now authenticate users with single sign-on (SAML) and require a login to see projects. Interrupted runs show as failed, and comparisons prefer reference runs on the same input.
entry.content:
QA-Board servers can now authenticate users with single sign-on (SAML) and require a login to see projects. Interrupted runs show as failed, and comparisons prefer reference runs on the same input.

Admins

Single sign-on with SAML

Besides local accounts and LDAP, users can now sign in through a SAML identity provider. Choose the method with QABOARD_LOGIN_TYPE (LOCAL, LDAP or SAML) and configure SAML with the QABOARD_SAML_* variables.

Learn more →
Admins

Require a login

Set QABOARD_LOGIN_REQUIRED=true to block anonymous users: they must sign in before opening a project.

Learn more →

Web app​

  • When matching runs with the reference, the web app and exports now prefer reference runs with the same input path.
  • Stopped batches now mark their interrupted runs as failed, with finer-grained statuses.

CLI and project setup​

  • qa batch --action-on-existing skip no longer skips runs that are still pending: it waits for them instead.
  • The LSF runner no longer uses fast_queue: jobs always go to the configured queue.
  • Absolute input paths are resolved through symlinks.
  • The package now depends on scikit-learn instead of the deprecated sklearn name.

Server and administration​

  • The public sign-up API endpoint is disabled, to prevent unauthorized users from creating accounts.
  • The login settings are baked into the web app image when it is built.
  • nginx forwards the X-Forwarded-* headers that SAML needs, and the development setup can run over HTTPS.
  • The cleanup job falls back to deleting the whole output directory when a run has no file manifest.

Documentation​

  • The server setup page documents user management, sign-in methods and the new login variables.

Fixes​

  • Fixed a directory traversal vulnerability in the nginx configuration for the docs.
  • Fixed regions of interest when the image is zoomed, and the text copied from the ROI viewer.
